div.head: III Atr 7.1
div.ab: Gif he clæne beo æt þam ordale, nime úpp his mǽg; gif he þonne ful beo, licge þar he lǽg, ⁊ gilde an C.
Si mundus sit in ordalio, diffodiat cognatum suum; si uero sit immundus, iaceat ipse fur ubi iacebat, et alius reddat.
Gif he clæne beo æt þam ordale, nime úpp his mǽg; gif he þonne ful beo, licge þar he lǽg, ⁊ gilde an C.

Wenn er rein erfunden ist bei dem Ordal, so nehme er [jenen] seinen Verwandten herauf [aus unehrlichem Grabe]; wenn er dagegen schuldig erfunden ist, liege dieser wo er lag, und büsse er ein Hundert [Silbers].
If he is found clean at the ordeal, let him take up his kinsman [from the dishonoured grave]; but if he is found guilty, let [the kinsman] lie where he lay, and let him pay one hundred [of silver].

And if he prove innocent at the ordeal, he shall remove his kinsman [from his grave in unconsecrated ground]. If, however, he be guilty, the thief shall lie where he is, and he himself shall pay 100 [of silver].

And if he is proved right at the ordeal, he is to take up his kinsman [from unconsecrated ground]; if he, however, is proved wrong, [the slain thief] is to lie where he lay before, and he himself is to pay a hundred [of silver].

note.seg: This interpretation follows Liebermann. Presumably the supposed thief had been slain, cf. ECf. 36–36, 5 (Liebermann, i. p. 666 ff.).

note.label: right
note.seg: literally, “if he be clean”. Liebermann seems to take the pronoun to refer to the thief, but the text “Ordeal” uses the term “clean” to describe that condition of the hand three days after the ordeal which ensured victory for the man who had undergone it.
